gaps.fact: Some Mediterranean climates (warm air from the east): the Codex rightly calls the warm eastern air Pannonian, and keeps Mediterranean for Styria's Illyrian influence in the steiermark article only, but i-412fz5st marks Mediterranean wrong for that eastern air and no chapter tells a candidate how the Court's word maps onto the Codex's.
New oak is rarely used for Austrian white wine: it stands only as a wrong option in i-vmltc0f5 and in the article's cellar notes, never as a chapter fact or a key.
Kremstal DAC lies along the Krems river and Kamptal DAC along the Kamp, both tributaries of the Danube: only the article says so; i-k15cmcha names the town of Krems, not the river.
None of the Court's six (Emmerich Knoll, Rudi Pichler, FX Pichler, Prager, Schloss Gobelsburg, Bründlmayer) is ever a key in either bank; Rudi Pichler appears nowhere in the Codex at all.

Grüner Veltliner as the unoaked, crisp partner for fresh seafood, smoked fish, vegetables, herbs, fresh cheeses, schnitzel, and the hard foods asparagus and artichoke: no question in either bank pairs Grüner Veltliner with anything, and neither Austria chapter has a pairing line.

courtUpdates.printed: - Kamptal DAC: Along the Kampt River (a tributary of the Danube). Dry whites using Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.
courtUpdates.now: From the 2025 vintage Kamptal DAC wine must come from vineyards certified organic or certified under Sustainable Austria, an amendment published by the European Commission in 2025; the Codex does not yet carry it. The same search reports changes to the Leithaberg, Weinviertel, Kremstal and three Styrian DAC rules whose detail it did not give, and the replacement of the regional wine committees by producer associations from 2027, which will date c-v0n7g87c's 'the region's own wine committee drafts it'.
courtUpdates.source: Search: the EU amendment notice for the Kamptal PDO (eur-lex, C/2025/2992) and the trade report of wein.plus on six DAC regions.

notes: Mapped questions: Régionale 57 (Austria), Village 26 (Austria), 83 in all. Both columns are well served on law: the four tiers, the DAC idea with its two ladders, the Wachau's Steinfeder, Federspiel and Smaragd with their alcohol lines and the Vinea Wachau, the banderole, Kabinett as a Qualitätswein class, Ausbruch as Rust's alone, and the 2023 decree that makes Erste Lage and Grosse Lage legal (signed in June 2023, two months before the guide, so not logged as an update; the search found no published list of officially classified sites yet). The thin cells are the producer roll (none asked, Rudi Pichler absent), Grüner Veltliner at the table, the Krems and Kamp rivers, the rarity of new oak and the Court's word Mediterranean. The Court prints Wein among its Certified regions where Wien is meant, and Schloss Gobelsberg and the Kampt River for Gobelsburg and the Kamp; the Codex spells all three correctly. No factual error found: Zweigelt of 1922 from St. Laurent and Blaufränkisch, Grüner Veltliner from Traminer and St. Georgen, the 1985 scandal, Vinea Wachau 1983, Wachau DAC 2020, Weinviertel DAC 2002, Mittelburgenland the first red DAC, the Styrian DACs of 2018, Thermenregion 2023 completing the roster of eighteen, Leithaberg red at 85 per cent Blaufränkisch, Wiener Gemischter Satz at three varieties with none above half, and Sekt Austria renamed from Klassik in 2022 (confirmed by the second search) all hold. One house rule note for the owner: four Village explanations use a spaced single hyphen where a dash would stand (c-v0n7g87c, c-z0d3nt5o, c-7qte1nlo and c-xhb310kr: a hyphen with a space either side, round a parenthesis or before a gloss), which the dash rule forbids in spirit; a comma or a colon would serve. Two searches spent: the official site classification, and DAC and Sekt changes.
